brands.name: Proctor
brands.short_description: Custom surfboards built to order by Todd Proctor at his Ventura, California factory — retro, fish, groveler, shortboard, midlength, longboard, and gun models.

models.name: Funner
models.description: A great board for the surfer who wants the paddling ease of a longer board with the responsiveness of a shorter board. A good beginner board; or for the surfer making the transition from Longboard to Shortboard; or for those who don’t want to resort to a Longboard, but are finding their Shortboard is getting to be more work than fun.

models.name: Classic Noserider
models.description: Same like wut ‘da Classic Longboard….. but with a teardrop outline and a fuller nose; designed for tip time in the classic sense. Features 50/50 rails, rolled vee bottom, scoop in the nose; built for trim speed and dangling toes. Also available with volan cutlaps, knee paddle patches, cloth inlays, acid splashes, resin swirls, tail blocks, nose blocks, pigment opaques, tints, pinline art, gloss and polish….you name it we do it.

models.name: Rocket 88
models.description: A board that uses it’s extra weight to drive it into sweeping bottom turns, and uses a fast rocker and no-catch 50/50 rails to bolt clean down the line. The convex over the fin transitions the board from rail-to-rail in committed speed arcs. And that’s what the ‘Rocket 88’ is all about.

models.name: Lacerator
models.description: Sounds so sinister doesn’t it?…well, not to worry, it’s all in the name of aggressive fun. This is a good waves board, and perfect for rippers who want a board that can handle being pushed hard and fast through a myriad of edge-of-the-envelope maneuvers. It’s got a smooth entry rocker; no real flip, so it glides into waves and gets down the line quick and easy.

models.name: Accelerator L.E.
models.description: Basically the same overall design as the original Accelerator, but with all the entry rocker dropped super low. This works surprisingly well as the board gains a whole new easy trim speed and glide between maneuvers. This is something kind of lost in surfing right now, and I’ve noticed with all the high flying super rad maneuvers that there is some weird wide stance wiggling going on that in my opinion is looks ugly.

models.name: Howitzer
models.description: For as big of waves as you dare to paddle into. A Waimea, Todos Santos, Mavericks style gun . . . for deep water big wave spots. Made with plenty of volume for paddle speed to get in early, a rocker to handle long, steep drops and a vee bottom that bolts, driving through perilous troughs.

models.name: Archangel
models.description: New supersnarler gigantotubos model: the “Archangel”….beware forces of darkness, there is far more power in the light. 9’8″ x 20 1/2″ x 3 5/8” This gun had a more relaxed entry rocker, and a fuller nose outline for early glide in. It features volume forward under the chest for digging up heaps of speed in paddle, a beak nose cuz their cool and keep the nose down, and a traditional vee to flat to panel vee bottom aka Pat Curren / Brewer-esque hull for predictability and smooth glide.

models.name: West Peak
models.description: A gun for double overhead and bigger; typically a travel board unless you live in Mainland Mexico, the North Shore, or somewhere like that. Perfect for the days where the playing field is large-scale and there is “a lot” of water moving. The West Peak surfs top-to-bottom like a shortboard while maintaining the paddling and stability necessary to get in the waves early and drive hard turns in maxxing conditions.

models.name: Circa '86
models.description: Can you believe there is actually an 80’s model…I’m feeling old. Actually, I was a grom in the 80’s and what a great time it was; in part due to board design – less work for more speed; surfing didn’t have to be so technical back then and it seemed like there were less knee injuries… I don’t know?

models.name: The Sickle
models.description: This isn’t your grand daddy’s single fin…. it’s a high performance mono-fin sickle. It uses double barrel concaves under the front foot and channels out the back for speed and drive. The progressive rocker allows for modern style top-to-bottom surfing. If you like the feel of drawing clean, long-driving bottom turns… then the harvest is ripe.

models.name: SR-71
models.description: Features single-to-double concave bottom for a drivey, predictable feel. Lower entry allows you to get into waves early and gain quick bursts of speed down the line. Good amount of tail rocker bending through the second half of the board makes for a tight turning, top-to-bottom board.

models.name: Pipecleaner
models.description: A gun for hollow, powerful barrels. This one has a rolled vee in the nose that transitions to extreme, accelerated panel vees through the tail to feel right at home when hangin’ deep with the foamball. All guns customized according to surfer’s build & size/shape of waves to be surfed.

models.name: Greased Rascal
models.description: For those of you who have a near and dear place in your heart for the exuberant speed and summertime fun-ness of the Rascal….here is the new stepchild with nitrous oxide boosters added. Slide into waves earlier, zip through the crumble-flats and nail a nice feathery little lip over and over….without having to think too hard to smile it up.

models.name: TwinStitch
models.description: This twin fin right here has a lot of people talking. This latest variant of the performance twin fin model is bringing new, flourishing, joy/filled life and health and glide and speed and free-ness with grip and buckets of glory galore…it’s called the #Twinstitchsurfboard and it uses the bottom line and rocker of the #Zipstitchsurfboard combined with the outline and rails of the #Twinturbinesurfboard / a wider nose, narrower tailed, single-wing swallow with a slot channel through the tail for e

models.name: PostMod
models.description: This board combines a modernized, sleeked up retro fish outline with a progressive rocker and one-of-a-kind freaky hull contours. Glide or gouge, float or carve, crouch low with five on the nose, or stand tall and arch the back. Introducing a new rocker and hull contours to the traditional fish outline.

models.name: G4-71
models.description: Versatile, user-friendly easyrippin’ performance board. Moderate to low drivey rocker, yet still nice and whippy. A board you don’t have to think too much on…it just goes like a horse out tha gate. If you need to get just one performance board to see you through, this is the one to get.

models.name: Lil' Rascal
models.description: This squatty firebrand has all the speed of a retro-style shape, but with the holding power of a modern board. Using a bulby outline with a flatter rocker, full boxy rails, and new generation hull contours; it loves to rocket on 2 foot gutless days when most people are running for their longboards.

models.name: Big Rascal
models.description: The ultimate big guy fish surfboard. **All boards in the Rascal series can be built with larger dims to allow for the much loved performance features of the Rascals but with more volume where it’s appropriate for your needs. Just click on any Rascal series board in our online shop and select from the larger dimensions to make yours a “Big Rascal” This squatty firebrand has all the speed of a retro-style shape, but with the holding power of a modern board.

models.name: RascSqueak
models.description: A Rascal nose with a wider Pipsqueak rear & Pipsqueak flip nose. Short, wide and flat for speeding across weak waves. It uses a unique hydrofoilized jetstream hull and trenched-out, scalloped ‘sluice-box’ concaves; with down rail for going Ahwooooooooooo

models.name: Rascal II
models.description: Yes, you guessed correctly; the Rascal II is an offspring of the original Lil’ Rascal. Don’t worry, it’s not meant to replace the trusty, tried and true design of the original Rascal…. It started as just some thoughts…..ideas for a new board design after contemplating just how much fun I’d had on my Lil’ Rascal over the last year and a half.

models.name: Lil' Spuddy
models.description: The much loved Lil’ Rascal with a round tail This squatty firebrand has all the speed of a retro-style shape, but with the holding power of a modern board. Using a bulby outline with a flatter rocker, full boxy rails, and new generation hull contours; it loves to rocket on 2 foot gutless days when most people are running for their longboards.

models.name: Hideoscillous
models.description: ie. Hideous Oscillations from the Latin root hideous to the eye, yet one possessing beautiful oscillating motions in the water. An extreme combination of modern hull contours produces the glide of ‘free-friction’ between turns which intersects with the hold of a back foot ‘clamp’. A pedal-to-the-metal bear down of ultimate gougeability through maneuvers.

models.name: Pavarotti
models.description: It’s a new addition to the lineup this year, called the Pavarotti surfboard. This is a high performance uber-groveller, but it’s also is a great all around everyday board that catches waves easy with a fuller nose and lower entry rocker. Ridden roughly the same dimensions as a Monsta surfboard or an inch shorter.

models.name: Monstroscillous
models.description: features the stringerline center rocker of the Hideoscillous with a touch more entry rocker added to corner tight and dynamic, a fuller nose a la the Pavote (like a fuller outlined Monsta) with a wider steep hipsquash (kinda like a Curren tail from back in the day), and coupled with a jetstream heavy concave bottom that runs deep scalloped duals through the fins for back foot drive hold and acceleration like a hydrofoil.

models.name: Falcon v2
models.description: Falcon II double wing swallowtail (extreme reverse vee / spiral vee to drop rocker single cave with full barrel sluicebox inset double concaves splitting to a spiral vee fliptail compression chamber exhaust exit). The Falcon 2 is quickly becoming the most popular new board model with its extreme reverse vee to deep single spiralling doubles hull contour.

models.name: Back to the Future Twin Fin
models.description: This is THE BOARD for when it’s one foot and super grovel-town conditions. Mixing an 80’s style twinny outline with a very modern futuristic, hydro-harnessing hull contour. You wanna baffle longboarders and mid-lengthers till they shake their heads and cry?? Then hustle on to “hey I got it” town where the wave catchin’ is easy and the buckets are big.

models.name: The Bullet
models.description: Some people say, “Man, I’m tired of wiggling….I’m tired of my board sticking….I wanna go fast, I wanna feel free to speed and arc out my turns where I wanna.” These same people also say, “I don’t want to think no more ‘bout having to surf technical and perfect in the pocket….and having my board punish me if I don’t…..somebody gimme a bullet.” The bottom runs a single through the middle under the front foot for a positive drive off the front foot when the waves are small….then it splits to double

models.name: Greased Pig
models.description: A speed machine for chest high waves and smaller; this is the type of board that you drive like a race car….it’s going fast so all you gotta’ do is hang on and steer. It has a low entry rocker for quick paddling, ease catching waves, and increased lift in small/ flatter faced waves.

models.name: Flyin' Monsta
models.description: New for Fall ’18…The ever and oft-so-loved Monsta design with a new slightly pulled back outline and the extreme tail rocker and heavy single co ncave of the Flyin’ Lion applied to the bottom. A new super pockety, tail whipping, steep faced rail holding bucketer. The ‘one board quiver’.

models.name: ZipstaJet
models.description: swallow The latest iteration of our most oft loved “Monsta” model; a favorite for many years. It uses the centerline rocker of the Zipstitch with the outline of a swallowtail Monsta, the exaggeratedly deep and multi-scalloped concaves of the Jetstream and four short channels running off the tail.

models.name: Ghost
models.description: For those of you who like the Monsta, this is a high performance shortboard counterpart to that design. I’ve kept the rocker and bottom contours the same as that of the Monsta….so same speed, same positive flow…The outline, rail volume and deck foil is more “shortboardy, but with the wide point moved slightly forward & a bit fuller nose outline than a standard “needled out” perfect waves shortboard.

models.name: El Pavote
models.description: Best summed up – easy speed with maximum hold for performance surfing. El Pavote is basically the Falcon model with all the spiral vee through the back half of the board shaped out of the bottom; and replaced with a deep even single concave with subtle doubles running the length of the back 1/3 of the rocker and off the tail block.

models.name: Kookaburra
models.description: Named after a noisy, brightly colored bird from Australia; this board is designed to generate crazy speed at the drop of a hat, yet perform all the radical high flyin’ maneuvers of a high performance shortboard. A very versatile board that will take you wherever you wanna go whether it’s two foot and mushy or overhead and pumpin’.

models.name: Scarecrow
models.description: scary? no. this skinny-tailed-swabby is the way to go. Todd, after his first session on it, “…it felt like butter in a boiling hot pan…I think I did the best layback turn of my life on that board.” This is the fastest trim speed board ever. Ideal for pointbreaks, this board has incredible drive and projection down the line due to the fuller nose outline and low entry rocker.

models.name: MonstaPig
models.description: Monsta with Greased Pig v.4 rocker and bottom. Quickly becoming a popular everyday board. A versatile mid-range groveler that flies through the flats, yet runs crisp and clean in a good pocket.

models.name: Apex
models.description: An all-around high performance shortboard; a conglomeration of design aspects from the Blackbird, Super-Typhoon and Ghost models all synthesized into one versatile compact shape. The entry rocker is lower like that of the Ghost, allowing for early entry into waves and quick speed down the line.

models.name: Super-Typhoon
models.description: This has been a long-standing favorite for performance surfing when the waves get good. A perfect trip board. However, this year I’ve tweaked with the rocker a bit to give it that same good waves feel in less than perfect conditions. So, if you want a whippy fins-free, super high performance board that also holds a rail in a drawn out arc; then this is the one.

models.name: Flyin' Lion
models.description: A board that has a feeling of continuous on-rail motion taking natural lines that run cross-grain to the natural pull of the water flow on the wave face; letting you gain drive by a board that intrinsically wants to go hard on rail and turn grippy yet responsive in the steepest parts of the wave.

models.name: Superabound
models.description: A “good waves” dream board. Plenty of rocker with a consistent bend from nose to tail, and lots of concave running the length of the board. The best ‘trip’ board I make, or for when your local spot gets top to bottom. Features continuous curve throughout with a steady-running single-to-inset-double concave SuperAbound from the greek word hupernike , to excel still more Superabound step-up For gettin’ barrelled.

models.name: The Mendia
models.description: This board design is inspired by the surfing of madman Pete Mendia, for a powersurfing hackathon. A board designed for timeless power surfing; gouging rail arcs; big sprays; made for deep barrels and goliath turns. Crazy sweepy tail rocker for a waterworks spectacular. Any and all dims available.

models.name: Flyin' Pig
models.description: for the average head high to slightly overhead days, and for getting into the barrel easy and early, with a wide open sweet spot, a drivey board that will do crisp gafs in the pocket; an “easy” board that lets you get speed easy, but will also carve it up lightning fast..

models.name: Ante-Up
models.description: For when the waves are getting a bit bigger and punchier than your regular shortboard can handle. The Ante Up is that little extra you need to get into bigger waves easier and maintain the balance of speed and stability necessary to rip on the overhead dream days. The rocker has an even bend from nose to tail.

models.name: Performance Noserider
models.description: This board features a teardrop outline with a fuller nose to provide drive up front. A lower entry rocker and increased tail rocker keep it quick-trimming off the nose, yet loose off the tail. The bottom has a single concave under the nose that splits into double caves through the mid, and accelerates into a spiral vee through the last third of the board.

models.name: Classic Longboard
models.description: Well they’re classic – 50/50 rails, rolled vee bottom, scoop in the nose; Built for trim speed, walking the nose, drop knee turns…it’s a mellower era and the mood is flowin’. We do them with volan cutlaps, paddle patches, cloth inlays, acid splashes, resin swirls, tail blocks, nose blocks, pigment opques, tints, pinline art, gloss and polish…you name it we do it (even step decks…shhh – don’t tell anybody).

models.name: SuperFortress
models.description: A modern interpretation of the Classic Noserider a la Nuuhiwa era. Plenty of volume, heavy concave/scoop in the nose combined with a very low rocker from the tip through the belly makes for easy glidin’. No catch 50/50 rails allows smooth transitions in trim. Single fin with accelerated tail rocker lets it pivot like a more modern board, allowing easier positioning to setup for “the walk”.

models.name: SuperFortress Mod
models.description: For some time now, I’ve been seeing a need for a pig style classic longboard, and finally found a window of opportunity thanks to a 12 year old girl named Lily from Ventura, who ordered this special shape custom some time back. It uses the same rocker and bottom as the Superfortress / classic noserider, but the outline has been adjusted to a sleeker nose with the planshape’s wide point pulled back and added curve into the tailblock.

models.name: ZipStitch
models.description: A high performance groveler for detonating small waves. For zippin’ across and stitchin’ it up. A New Covenant / A New Kind of Surfing: For the everyday core score blue collar wave rider. Have you noticed how, even on the world tour, surfers are coming off of the bottom with way less on-rail drive than Tom Curren and Mark Occhilupo exhibited in the 80’s?

models.name: Sputnik
models.description: Small waves no problem; easy entry; rocket fuel down the line. Super fast, yet turns like a good performance board and holds a rail super good too which is new territory for these kinds of shapes. For ease of paddling, quick take-off, and getting more radical & vertical Post first surf from Todd….

models.name: Performance Longboard
models.description: The performance longboard features additional rocker, sleeker outline, and more tapered responsive rails. The bottom utilizes a concave in the nose for increased lift in noseriding, which transitions to a double concave through the mid-section of the board, then to a concave vee or “spiral vee” through the fins and last 1/3 of the board.

models.name: Manatee
models.description: Lots of shortboarders have been jumping on this thing and raving. Mini so you can shwang it around easier than a longboard but still catch anything you want. Our laminator swears by his. The bottom utilizes a concave in the nose for increased lift in noseriding, which transitions to a double concave through the mid-section of the board, then to a concave vee or “spiral vee” through the fins and last 1/3 of the board.

models.name: MonstaFish
models.description: “Gut that fish” – the all new modern retroactive Twin/Quad Fang uses progressive rocker & deep heavy concaves for a board that gets up on plane, and holds a rail through full-speed carves like none before it. I’ve literally gutted the belly of the beast so she has more efficient water flow, making her speedy as all get out with no lack of fast-twitch muscle fiber rail response.

models.name: SuperGrom
models.description: How great is it to be a grom?!…surfin’ three sessions a day….the perpetual salt-bake on your skin…and too amped for that next surf, to push on to the next level with the new maneuvers you’ve been trying. Here’s a board for you core groms out there. This board’s as high performance as they come; scaled down to what’s the right dimensions for you.

models.name: Magnum Opus
models.description: A high performance average waves board that drives out of gouges with unbridled enthusiasm…disguised as an unassuming beak-nosed throw-back fishy groveller… I keep getting asked, “Hey, is there any footage of Rozsa on that new trippy little board?” Everybody has missed seeing Nick surf the last few years, as have I.

models.name: GrovelChief
models.description: Features wider nose outline and full tailblock for maximum glide and carry, with a less rockered version of the #Falcon2surfboard rocker and bottom for seemless ball-bearing rail to rail execution. Top speed surpasses previous redline markers, and holds a rail like a boss on wings.

models.name: MobstaChief
models.description: Born 5 lbs. 2 oz. and at 6’3 1/2” x 23” x 3 3/8” 55L …we welcome to the world the #MoBstaChief a new twin fin ala MR style for da big boys. It’s the #Monstachief with a fuller nose outline, single wing swallowtail, flat deck, down rail, beak nose twinny for mobbin’ like a boss when those knee to waist high days got you thinkin’ what a few extra horses might do to a Hemi engine.

models.name: The Blazer
models.description: Jetstream single to double concave to vee . . . and perimeter chimes For gliding and gouging like an Olympic discus; spinning, orbiting its way through any kind of wave, any kind of lineup

models.name: Derringer
models.description: A new very smooth and forgiving egg/hybrid/funshape design / perfect crossover for transitioning from longboard to short, or when you want the paddle ease of a bigger board but the performance characteristics of a shorter board…features a slight single to double with subtle spiral vee off the tail.

models.name: Displacement Hull
models.description: Ever glide along at full tilt speed trim and feel like your weightless? The Hull gets you there. Pictured Here: 7’0″ x 24″ x 3 1/4″ pintail

models.name: The Earthy Midlength
models.description: a 70’s throwback with modern accoutrement to zesty up the dish. What was I thinking? …. watch and see #earthymidlength

models.name: The Pelican Midlength
models.description: 6-channel / panel vee bottom we’re calling “The Pelican” because it glides and swoops smooth and silent as it speeds along its beaked nose way. Now available for custom orders for all you Morning of the Earth lovers…why? Because we love you 😉 This ones for a fella named Aric who’s 31, 5’11”, 190lbs.

models.name: Bullpin
models.description: Customized step-up for big rolly Steamer Lane and other cali points. 7’0″ x 19 5/8″ x 2 3/4″ 39L inverted fulcrum rocker with fuller ‘bull-ish’ nose outline to tear-dropping rounded pin…not too pinny so it can hold its speed through long drawn out open faced carves, yet drawn in enough to fit steep and deep and hold a line through barrel sections.

models.name: Monstachief
models.description: Specifically designed for guys in the 180 – 300lbs + range that want a versatile all-around board they can gouge away on…..in anything from 2 ft. sludge, to overhead throaters. Taken from the original monsta design, this board is armed with folkloric dimensions on a grand scale. For instance, the flagship of the line boasts 6’4″ x 21 1/2″ x 3 1/8″ with full, boxy rails; a 14 1/2″ wide nose and 16 1/2″ wide tail.

models.name: Big Chief
models.description: Developed specifically for heavier surfers and/or those that surf more off their rail; this is the shortboard you can rip on and not sink on. Heavier surfers and those that grew up surfing during the 80’s era tend to surf more with their rails than off their fins. So the fuller rails of this design are essential for a board that “pushes back” and drives through turns.

models.name: Tail Caves II
models.description: This shape has been refined from feedback at Australia’s Super Bank, Burleigh Heads and Kirra. This board loves the barrel and loves to gouge. The rocker features a fair amount of bend between the feet, shallow concaves through the fins and slight vee running off the back fin. If you want a board that throttles you maching out of deep caverns, and enjoy running a rail bucketing through vert benders…then this is the one for you.
